Q: JOIN subqueries containing COUNT() and SUM() expressions in a SELECT query using CodeIgniter's query builder A:

Here's effectively the query builder script for the joined subqueries presented in @GordonLinoff's answer. I don't think the outer GROUP BY clause is useful, so I removed it.

public function getReferralsAndEarnings(): array
{
    $referrals = $this->db
        ->select('inviter_id, COUNT(*) referrals')
        ->group_by('inviter_id')
        ->get_compiled_select('users');
    
    $earned = $this->db
        ->select('receiver_id')
        ->select_sum('amount', 'earned')
        ->group_by('receiver_id')
        ->get_compiled_select('transactions');
    
    return $this->db
        ->select('u.id, COALESCE(referrals, 0) referrals, COALESCE(earned, 0) earned')
        ->join("($referrals) r", 'r.inviter_id=u.id', 'left')
        ->join("($earned) e", 'e.receiver_id=u.inviter_id', 'left')
        ->order_by('referrals', 'desc')
        ->order_by('earnings', 'desc')
        ->get('users u')
        ->result();
}

Renders as:

SELECT `u`.`id`, COALESCE(referrals, 0) referrals, COALESCE(earned, 0) earned
FROM `users` `u`
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT `inviter_id`, COUNT(*) referrals
    FROM `users`
    GROUP BY `inviter_id`
) r ON `r`.`inviter_id`=`u`.`id`
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT `receiver_id`, SUM(`amount`) AS `earned`
    FROM `transactions`
    GROUP BY `receiver_id`
) e ON `e`.`receiver_id`=`u`.`inviter_id`
ORDER BY `referrals` DESC, `earnings` DESC

Q: iOS 26 Liquid Glass: Unwanted visual highlight on nearby glass elements when tapping a glass element A:

This is simply not how you should be using liquid glass in the first place, so it is no surprise that it behaves unexpectedly.

You should not place glass on top of other glass. Apple acknowledges this in WWDC 25 Meet Liquid Glass at 13:13:

Consider this tableview: making it Liquid Glass would make it compete with other elements and muddy the hierarchy. So keep it in the content layer instead to ensure clarity. Similarly, always avoid glass on glass. Stacking Liquid Glass elements on top of each other can quickly make the interface feel cluttered and confusing.

As you have observed, pressing on the FAB causes the glass at the back to be highlighted as well, which is "confusing", exactly as Apple said.

Also at 13:03, it is also said that

You may be tempted to use Liquid Glass everywhere but it is best reserved for the navigation layer that floats above the content of your app.

The glass cards in the scroll view look very much like it displays your app's content, and therefore should be placed in the content layer. This is similar to the table view mentioned in the WWDC video.

Consider creating the cards using standard materials such as .thinMaterial instead.

Q: Problems linking boost with cmake: undefined reference to boost::program_options A:

You are using old CMake code patterns. You should not use include_directories anymore. Use modern CMake and let target_link_libraries with proper arguments of targets do this job (it will link library and setup includes at the same time).

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10.0)
project(test_opencv VERSION 0.1.0 LANGUAGES C CXX)

find_package(OpenCV REQUIRED)
message(STATUS " OpenCV Version: ${OpenCV_VERSION}")

find_package(Boost 1.4.0 COMPONENTS program_options REQUIRED)
message(STATUS " Boost Version: ${Boost_VERSION}")

add_executable(test_opencv main.cpp)

# apparently OpenCV do not provide nice cmake alias like other libraries
# target_link_libraries(test_opencv PUBLIC OpenCV::OpenCV)
# so here is working version:
target_include_directories(test_opencv PUBLIC ${Boost_INCLUDE_DIRS})
target_link_libraries(test_opencv PUBLIC ${OpenCV_LIBS})

# this one I'm using and it works.
target_link_libraries(test_opencv PUBLIC Boost::program_options)

Tested it works on my machine.

Q: Setting the statement name in PDO Prepared Statements (MySQL/MariaDB) A:

Caching prepared SQL statements (PREPARE name FROM ...) generally doesn’t make sense.

Prepared statements are session-local

Each connection has its own prepared statement namespace: a PREPARE name exists only for the current session. You cannot share prepared statements across connections.

Attempting to “cache prepared statements globally” is tricky. You would need to query performance_schema.prepared_statements_instances to see if the statement exists and belongs to your thread, i.e., match OWNER_THREAD_ID to your connection’s THREAD_ID via performance_schema.threads.

Even then, the performance_schema information is limited: it does not reveal metadata locks, pending result sets, or previous errors. You also cannot be sure the statement is still valid (e.g., if the underlying table has been dropped or altered).

Executing a prepared statement still requires extra setup

Each execution may require setting and binding variables, depending on the query.

These extra network round trips can partially offset the benefits of “preparing once.”

The performance benefit is usually small

MySQL/MariaDB still perform checks on table metadata, permissions, etc., on every execution.

In simple benchmarks, the difference between PREPARE once + EXECUTE and EXECUTE IMMEDIATE is typically very small (~4%).

Considering the added complexity of caching and checking performance_schema, such a solution will be actually slower and less stable.

Suggestion: Do not use PREPARE FROM sql statements for caching purposes. Instead, use prepared statements via the binary protocol, and close them as soon as they are no longer needed.

Q: How to use jq to output JSONL (one independent JSON object per line) A:

I found an easier way to read jsonl below

  • JSONL → JSON

    jq -s '.' input.jsonl > output.json

  • JSON → JSONL

    jq -c '.[]' input.json > output.jsonl

Sources

  • https://gist.github.com/sloanlance/c3bf746b6396f60d321f5535e1ced892

  • https://github.com/jqlang/jq/wiki/Cookbook#jsonl-%EF%B8%8E-json-conversion
